_README: conductor-oss known failures for the agent python e2e suite (bundle: conductor-ai-e2e-python-*, from conductor-oss/python-sdk), consumed by known_failures_plugin.py via E2E_KNOWN_FAILURES. Each key is a pytest node-id (or a '<file>::<Class>::<test>' suffix); the value is the reason + tracking link. The gate stays green by xfail-ing these; a key that matches nothing is a harmless no-op (the test still runs and the gate still catches a real break), and a fixed bug turns its test XPASS — remove the entry then. Do NOT list flaky tests (rerun handles those). The plugin reports each entry's match count and raises a KnownFailuresWarning when an entry matches 0 tests (stale/typo'd) or more than 1 (over-broad), so a mis-written key is visible in the log rather than silent. NOTE: adding an entry moves a test out of the PASSED column, so E2E_MIN_PASSED in ci.yml must be lowered by the same amount in the same commit — otherwise the passed-count floor fails the lane for an unrelated-looking reason.
_HOWTO: Reconcile from the run's results/junit-e2e.xml. A value is either a reason string (test still RUNS so it XPASSes when fixed) or an object {"reason":..., "run":false} to xfail WITHOUT executing (use for a deterministic hang that would burn CI time; un-list it manually when fixed). Example: "test_suite4_mcp_tools.py::TestSuite4McpTools::test_mcp_lifecycle": "reason — conductor-oss/conductor#NNNN"
_CONTEXT_cli_skills: The 3 Suite16 entries below cover the SERVER-SIDE skills registry (/api/skills — register/list/get/pull/delete of agentspan skill packages). NOT to be confused with 'Conductor Skills' in docs/devguide/how-tos/conductor-skills.md, which teaches AI coding agents to drive Conductor and is unrelated. conductor-oss does not support the server-side skills API: SkillController is gated on BOTH conductor.integrations.ai.enabled AND agentspan.skills.enabled, and the latter has no default in application.properties and is set in exactly one place repo-wide — AgentSpanDeploymentContractEndToEndTest, which opts in explicitly. So /api/skills is off in every real deployment and POST /api/skills/register returns 404. History, for anyone tracing it: #1288 (commit 011040107, first in v3.32.0-rc.9) added the second gate prop; before that these passed on rc.8, which is what python-sdk pins. These are NOT a bug to fix — they are an unsupported feature. These tests DO run (the lane provisions the agentspan CLI they shell out to — it is load-bearing for the credential suites' skip path, so it cannot be dropped to make these skip instead), and they stay xfail-ed here. If server-side skills ever become supported, boot the server with agentspan.skills.enabled=true and delete these entries — they will XPASS. Tracking: conductor-oss/conductor#1353.

test_suite21_scheduling.py::TestDelete::: get_schedule() on a deleted schedule is expected to return None, but conductor-oss answers GET /api/scheduler/schedules/{name} with 404 and the SDK's OrkesSchedulerClient.get_schedule propagates it as ApiException(404) instead of translating to None. Surfaced when SCHEDULER_CONDUCTOR_URL was pointed at the conductor-oss server — the other 10 tests in the suite pass. Server/SDK contract mismatch on the not-found case; decide whether the server should return 200/null or the SDK should map 404 -> None.

test_suite14_stateful_domain.py::TestSui.reason: Stateful swarm never completes; workflow ends TIMED_OUT. ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-07-29 after reproducing locally — the earlier note here blamed #1356 for dropping the swarm transfer task defs, and that is wrong on every link: the SDK registers them fine ('Registered task definition' for all 6 *_transfer_to_*), the 'No such task by name <agent>_transfer_to_<other>' server lines are the SDK's benign lookup-before-create, and the handoff itself succeeds (agent 0's sub-workflow reaches COMPLETED including transfer_msg). What actually hangs is a TOOL worker. AgentRuntime._register_workers reads `agent.stateful` on the immediate agent only, but the test attaches swarm_tool to the swarm MEMBERS (swarm_agent_a/_b), which are not themselves stateful — so the tool worker registers with domain=None while the stateful swarm makes the server domain-route the task (taskToDomain maps swarm_tool -> the session domain). The task is queued in the domain queue with nothing polling it: pollCount=0, startTime=0, the FORK's JOIN never satisfies, and the workflow times out. Second, independent bug behind it: the test's own _find_tasks_by_type matches only taskDefName, but handoff_check is emitted as an INLINE task whose taskDefName is literally 'INLINE' — so `assert handoff_tasks` fails even though 20 handoff_check tasks exist and are COMPLETED. Both fixes are in python-sdk, not this repo: propagate statefulness to member agents in _register_workers (and the matching gap in ConfigSerializer._serialize_agent), and match referenceTaskName in the test helper. Verified locally against the pinned 2.0.0-rc2: stock = FAILED (RUNNING, 304s); SDK fix only = COMPLETED but fails the handoff_check assert; both fixes = PASSED in 118s. Timing note: a single attempt is ~304s (the SDK's 300s wait), not ~908s — that figure was three attempts under conftest's unconditional flaky(reruns=2). run:false keeps ~15min off every CI run while it stands; once a python-sdk release carries the fixes, bump the bundle pin, delete this entry and raise E2E_MIN_PASSED by 1 (it will PASS, not XPASS, since run:false cannot xpass). Tracking: conductor-oss/conductor#1363.
